subject: Post-call recap: Horizon Health decision criteria & smoke probes
messages:

Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Thanks for the demo earlier — quick note with what matters most for us right now.

Highlights from our side:
- Latency under 80ms p95 for chat path with 512-token context (user-facing SLA).
- Support for private VPC deployment and KMS integration — HIPAA-ish controls required.
- Predictable per-session cost: we need guidance on batching/quantization tradeoffs.

Open questions we promised to share: provider comparisons (latency/cost), smoke tests to validate KV-cache behavior, and recommended rollback plan if model performance regresses.

Sahil
Director, Engineering
Horizon Health

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Appreciate the clear priorities, Sahil — and great questions. Short recap from our side plus next steps so we all have alignment.

Recap of pain points you shared:
- User-facing latency target: p95 <= 80ms for 512-token interactive sessions.
- Strict data controls: VPC deployment + customer-managed KMS required.
- Cost predictability: need per-session cost modelling and knobs to tune quality vs spend.

How Redwood maps to those needs (summary):
- Serving runtime can operate in your VPC with KMS/HSM integration; we have a private deployment package and audit logging.
- We can target p95 60-75ms on our dedicated L4 profile for the model family you saw; exact numbers depend on sequence distribution and batching.
- Redwood Optimize will produce a recommended batching/quantization profile and an estimated per-session cost range.

Competitive snapshot (quick):
- Provider A: good latency but limited private deployment features; weak in audit logging.
- Provider B: robust security but higher per-token cost; limited guidance on batching/quantization.
- Redwood: strong runtime telemetry, native fallback routing, and tooling to trade cost vs quality with measurable evals.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) We’ll share a short smoke-test plan (KV-cache, prefix latency, failover) by EOD today.
2) Redwood will run a baseline latency/cost profile in our hosted tenant and share a heatmap for your 3 test prompts.
3) Agree on a 10-day smoke test where Horizon runs in a dedicated sandbox (VPC) and we correlate logs.

Can Priya and Sahil confirm availability for the kickoff on Thu 7/1 at 10am PT?

Marcus Lin
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

--
Attachment: "redwood-bakeoff-checklist.pdf" (pdf stub)

Thanks Marcus — that framing helps. Two clarifications from procurement/security: 
1) We need a short list of required network ports and expected IP ranges for the sandbox VPC.
2) We'd like to understand what data residency guarantees Redwood can provide for logs and KV cache — retention policy and deletion process.

Also, we've been asked to validate vendor claims against Provider A and Provider C; can you include an objective checklist we can run? Procurement will want to see a simple pass/fail table.

I'm available for the Thu 7/1 10am PT kickoff.

Best,
Priya Sethi
Sr. Procurement Manager | Horizon Health

Hi all — joining to outline the proposed smoke tests and acceptance criteria so procurement/security can run the pass/fail checklist. See plan below and let us know if anything should be added.

Smoke test plan (10-day sandbox):
- Test A: KV-cache persistence and prefix hit-rate across cold-starts (target: >90% prefix hit on typical flows).
- Test B: P95 latency for 512-token chat path under 100 RPS burst (target: <=80ms p95).
- Test C: Failover behavior between model variants (inject simulated spike to trigger fallback routing).
- Test D: Audit/logging export and deletion workflow (confirm retention window and manual deletion flow).

Acceptance criteria (simple pass/fail):
- Pass if target thresholds met for 3/4 tests and no unresolved security blockers.

Deliverables we will provide before kickoff:
- Detailed smoke-test checklist (spreadsheet with exact commands/requests).
- IP / port list for sandbox VPC and minimal firewall rules.
- A short write-up on KV-cache residency and deletion APIs.

If that aligns, Marcus and Camila will own the test instrumentation and we'll provide daily test summaries. Marcus — want to put owners on each test?

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
